- When sentiment turns bullish (↑ sentiment change) and news volume spikes, model tends to overreact and overshoot true price — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is neutral or bearish (↓ sentiment change) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects — adjust downward by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price during high news volume periods — increase forecast by 1–3% for each 1.0+ news volume unit.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often fails to capture momentum decay — apply a 1–3 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment is flat or mixed (±0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise — use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
- Model tends to underestimate true price in late-cycle (e.g., 2024-12) — apply a 2–4% upward bias for end-of-year or high-sentiment periods.
